newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Verbund says rejig to bring big savings.
newsitem.headline: Verbund says rejig to bring big savings.

text.p: Austrian national grid company Oesterreichische Elektrizitaetswirtschafts AG (Verbund) said on Friday restructuring next year should bring annual savings of around one billion schillings from the year 2000.
Following the reorganisation in January 1997, a holding company will oversee four previously separate divisions, including electricity generation and supply.

Verbund has said the plan, which involves 500 job losses by the end of 1998, will slim management by 40 percent and get the firm into shape for the liberalisation of EU energy markets at the end of the century.
"The new way of dividing operations into areas of business will save the company one billion schillings a year from 2000," chief executive Johann Haider told journalists.

He reinforced Verbund's interest in buying into regional electricity suppliers but declined to give details. Upper Austrian utility OKA and Styrian electricity firm STEWEAG are amongst the government's sell-off candidates. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
